$comment: Copy this to deploy.config.<name>.json (gitignored) and fill in your own values, then: node scripts/deploy.mjs deploy.config.<name>.json
$comment_domains: Recommended domain layout (see README 'Custom domains'): the SPA lives at your bare apex domain (your-domain.example), the API gets its own subdomain (sharing-api.your-domain.example), and Cognito gets its own too (sharing-auth.your-domain.example). Keeps each piece independently swappable and avoids CloudFront path-routing entirely.
$comment_resourcePrefix: MUST be unique from every other deployment in this same AWS account (or use a different 'stage') -- it names the DynamoDB tables and the auto-generated Cognito domain, both of which collide with another deployment's if this matches. Usually just your space name.
$comment_customDomains: Both optional -- omit either/both to use the auto-generated amazoncognito.com domain and/or the raw execute-api.amazonaws.com URL instead. Each needs its own ACM cert + DNS record set up OUTSIDE this config first -- see README 'Custom domains' for the one-time manual steps (a domain only you control, can't be scripted generically).
$comment_adopt: Omit the whole 'adopt' block for a brand-new space (fresh Cognito pool + tables). Only set it if you're pointing this stack at an EXISTING pool (see README 'Adopt mode').
$comment_oauth: Omit 'google'/'facebook' entirely for email/password-only sign-in. When present, the actual client secret is pulled from SSM at deploy time -- never put a secret value directly in this file. See README step 2 for creating these SSM parameters.
$comment_frontend: Omit entirely to only deploy the backend. When present, builds the SPA and syncs it to the S3/CloudFront infra named by distributionStackName (see README 'Deploy the frontend infra' -- must already exist). apiBase is optional -- when omitted, it's derived automatically from apiCustomDomainUrl (or the raw ApiEndpoint if you didn't set up a custom API domain).
